title: What Does the Bible Say About Reincarnation? 26 Verses
description: Does the Bible teach reincarnation? Verses on death and judgment, Elijah and John the Baptist, being born again and the resurrection.
keywords: what does the bible say about reincarnation
summary: The word reincarnation does not appear in the World English Bible or the King James Version (0 verses). Hebrews 9:27 is the verse most often cited against it: 'it is appointed for men to die once, and after this, judgment.' Verses sometimes cited for reincarnation, such as Jesus calling John the Baptist Elijah (Matthew 11:13-14, 17:10-13) and the question about a man born blind (John 9:1-3), are explained in the text itself: John came 'in the spirit and power of Elijah' (Luke 1:17), and Jesus answers that the blindness was not caused by an earlier sin. The Bible's teaching is a single life followed by resurrection and judgment (John 5:28-29, 1 Corinthians 15:42-44). The verses below set out both sides of the passages.

faqs.a: No. Hebrews 9:27 says people die once and then face judgment, and the Bible's hope for the dead is resurrection, not return in another body (1 Corinthians 15:42-44, John 11:25-26).

faqs.q: Was John the Baptist Elijah reborn?
faqs.a: Jesus says John is the Elijah who was to come (Matthew 11:14), yet John himself says he is not Elijah (John 1:21). Luke 1:17 resolves it: John came in the spirit and power of Elijah, fulfilling the role without being the same person.

faqs.q: What does being born again mean?
faqs.a: Jesus tells Nicodemus that one must be born of water and the Spirit (John 3:3-7), and Peter says believers are born again by the word of God (1 Peter 1:23). It describes spiritual new life in this life, not a new body after death.

faqs.q: What does the Bible say happens after death?
faqs.a: Believers are with Christ (Philippians 1:23, 2 Corinthians 5:8), then raised with new bodies (1 Corinthians 15:51-53), and everyone faces judgment (2 Corinthians 5:10, Hebrews 9:27).
